markdown_content: ## Fur strand visibility in the 3D window (CLO 2026.0) This section explains how to display fur strands in the 3D viewport using the **Fur Strand** option, and how to control this via **User Settings**. It also clarifies the difference between **Fur Strand** and **Fur Render** visibility in the 3D window. - In the **3D window**, switch the fur display mode to **fur strand** to see strand detail directly in the viewport. - If you use **fur render**, the fur strands won’t be visible in the **3D** window (you’ll mainly see fur in the render output). - User control: - Go to **User Settings** (top of the settings area). - Adjust the fur strand display setting. - Viewport navigation: - In **3D**, locate **Fur Strand Shape** and choose the suggested option **Plain**. ## Using Z offsets to place graphics above fur (pineapple mask example) This section covers how to position a graphic so it appears on top of fur while creating an automatic cutout/mask in the fur. It uses the example of a **pineapple** graphic and focuses on aligning **Z offsets** to fix placement in the 3D view. - Workflow: 1. Open the **Graphic** tab. 2. Select and add the **pineapple** graphic. 3. Resize and rotate as needed (e.g., “pineapple-ing it”). 4. Adjust placement in the **3D** window using **Z offsets**. - Key placement behavior: - After matching the correct **Z offsets**, the graphic sits on top of the fur in the 3D viewport. - The fur automatically creates a **mask/cutout** where the graphic sits. - Example values mentioned: - For the pineapple graphic, **Z offset** was set to **0.7** in **Edit Pineapple**. - The presenter also references matching a value to **0.80** to correct 3D positioning (then the placement “fixes itself” in the 3D window). - Verification in render: - In the **Render** window, the cutout/mask is visible and the fur updates automatically. - The presenter notes they didn’t wait for a full render, but the interactive view already shows the masking working correctly. ## Fur seam trimming controls (Thickness + Gradation) This section describes the new **fur trimmer** seam controls available in the **Edit Sewing Tool**. It explains how **Thickness** and **Gradation** affect how much seam fur is visible, including numeric ranges and practical differences. - Steps: 1. Open **Edit Sewing Tool**. 2. Select seam groups (example: **all sleeve seams**). - The presenter uses **Shift** to select multiple seams. 3. In the **Property Editor**, find the new **fur trimmer** option. - Parameters: - **Thickness** - Higher values push the seam fur visibility outward more. - Lower values reduce separation and visibility. - **Gradation** - Controls smoothness of the transition. - Example interpretation given: - **0** gradation: abrupt change. - **100** gradation: smooth transition. - Demonstrated comparisons (3D + render): - Sleeve seam A: - **Thickness = 0.5** - **Gradation = 80** - Sleeve seam B: - **Thickness = 0.1** - **Gradation = 80** - Result: - The presenter shows a “dramatic difference” between the two thickness settings in the 3D window and render preview. - They emphasize that higher **Thickness** increases separation/emptiness and changes how much seam area is exposed, while **lower** gradation makes the transition less smooth. - Numeric limits mentioned: - **Maximum (Thickness)**: about **3.9** (also described as ~**3.999999**) - **Minimum (Thickness)**: **0.001** (presenter states “zero zero one”) - **Gradation range**: **0–100** - (The presenter also reiterates: “For thickness… heads up.”)
